book.Title: PVT-LOG - LEAD PROF - E.01
book.page:
USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] =====================================================================
I awoke this morning to a message in my inbox, we've been greenlit to move on with the final stages of Project LIEF.
Finally, a moment of true exposure for my recent experiments. A moment to be vindicated and recognized for the truly revolutionary deeds I've done here.

We've, with my guidance of course, synthesized several key compounds that hold the mechanisms neccesary to biological unlockings so incredible, that flesh might finally revere thought.
If we can perfect this solution, we can create a tonic that when taken, allows one to sculpt themselves with their very minds.
The only thing holding me back, are the nitwits they assigned me. Sure Dr. ######### has some genius when it comes to her ... its ... however that thing refers to themselves, chemical synthesis skills. But they're a bit too ... altruistic? Humble? All 'hypothetical trials before clinical trials.'
What a child.

Science Officer Yoltum's a lazy bum, doing only what they are told and not putting in the effort to explore beyond their ability. Ignorant boy.
Assistant Science Officer Xeveye is ... tolerable. They praise my incredible genius--as they should--and speak with utmost respect while in my presence and presumably outside of it as well. He's a bit naive. But, I'll allow his presence for now.

The rest of the crew are a bunch of fools. Drabble, empty heads that only follow directions. But I'll make use of this lot. My road to glory was paved with agonies, but it was worth it. It was worth the wait, the time, the sweat, the blood. The humiliation at the hands of this society.
I will be the herald of a new era.

book.Title: PVT-LOG - LEAD PROF - E.02
book.page:
USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] =====================================================================
Dr. ########, all dour-eyed, whining like a sheep over the "dangers" of the clinical experiments. We've kept our biosynthization methods within scope. Somewhat. And though yes some of the recent clinical test on the vermin have resulted in, how shall I say this, 'lively tumors.' We've managed to curt the cliffedge with our experiments. Sure, the cells are revolting against the forced reconstitution efforts. But the compound is ... dynamic. Dr. ######## says it could be a catastrophe, a "world ending event".
Ha ... what an imagination.
The girl thinks this place wouldn't be qaurantined and pyro-glassed to high-hell before that even happens. Fret not I say, we are one of the most secure and advanced biogenetics firms in the known galaxy, the military in our pockets offers security and personnel unrivalled by our peers. Perks like administrative freedoms, enhanced emenities, and a security force that could vaporize an armada. Some talking tumors aren't going to stop us, no-- me, from achieving the glory that I deserve. I accused the girl of being a coward, "how did you even become a scientist? too busy sticking hypotheticals to paper and never practicing the practical element!"
Got a good laugh out of me, and Dr. Xeveye.
The others were too focused on their work to grasp my humor.

I guess I can't be too hard on the child. They've proven to have the technical ability. All that pencil-pushing made her accurate at least, and she managed to crack the first and second compound thresholds we needed for the serum with ... unsettling ease.
If these idiots can maintain focus for a moment, we might actually finish this project within the projected time scope.

book.Title: PVT-LOG - LEAD PROF - E.03
book.page:
USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] =====================================================================
What are these ingrates doing? Today, that fool Yoltum fumbles his journal, knocks over a specimen beaker, and triggers a site-wide contamination alert. Forcing all of us to vacate the synthesis chambers and wait in the foyer. Now I’m hearing it's a five-day lockdown as they sterilize the room for safety measures.
I’ll admit, I was irate. Inconsolably so, even. Do these idiots not realize how far off this could set us from the deadline? Upper echelons will be breathing down our necks, wondering what is keeping us from providing results.
How I couldn’t find anyone with even a modicum of my vigilance is … disturbing. What is this realm coming too?

book.Title: PVT-LOG - LEAD PROF - E.04
book.page:
USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] =====================================================================
Two weeks, TWO! Fumbling about the damn lab, wondering why all of our equipment is falling apart, malfunctioning, giving false reports and god-knows what else!
These setbacks have pushed us back MONTHS, MONTHS I TELL YOU. When the Upper Echelons hear of this … no, they can’t know!
Though yes we have managed to synthesize more of the compound's base structure, these setbacks have slowed our progress to a snail’s-pace– … mind the Littorinians … I mean absolutely no offense with that.
Mm.
Something needs to be done, I’ll need to execute double-shifts, double our production speed.

book.Title: PVT-LOG - LEAD PROF - E.05
book.page:
{{White|USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] ======================================================================}}
High-Echelon reached out. It's over. My career, my chance at true prestige. To be recollected in the memories of others as I should be–a genius, a revolutionary.
They determined us incompetent by any standard. No one with our level of technology and clearance should be having issues like this. They’d alerted that all funding for the project will be stripped, my seat vacated, and the lab direction shifted to more … humanitarian needs.
Humanitarian. As the significant share of impudent flock mean anything to something like this. Like me!
Three days. Three days to at least finish the compound. It's impossible.
What do I do? My honor, my reverence … gone.
I wouldn’t be able to stomach it.

book.Title: PVT-LOG - LEAD PROF - E.06
book.page:
{{White|USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] ======================================================================}}
We did it. And it was all thanks to my newest friend, Dr. Xeveye. He might be a bumbling idiot, he might be about as clumsy as an inebriated ape. But he’s honest. He’s loyal. And that loyalty is what I needed.
He outed the little vixen, ########## to me. The trollop! It's been her this whole time. Hiding her intent the whole time, holding us back with those irrational little feelings of hers. I should have known something was happening. It was like everytime we made progress something would break down, an accident, a miscalculation.
It was her!
But now I hold the power, I explained the situation to High-Echelon–made my claim for a militarized response, insubordinates in a classified facility is a crime you know? And before I knew it, garrisons at my doorstep, at my behest. Locking these fools into their offices and forcing them to continue the work, orderly, without breaks, without a lick of incompetence and with utmost diligence.
I’ve promoted Professor Xeveye to be my main assistant and overseer of the facility. The rest have been placed in solitary until they complete their assignments. And for the crime of federal mutiny and subjugation?
Imprisonment, or death. Execution on the spot I hear nowadays.
A perfect punishment for these little imbeciles.

book.Title: PVT-LOG - LEAD PROF - E.???
book.page:
ssd {{White|USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] ======================================================================}}
I’ve done it, I’ve commanded flesh to obey me, welded bone to my will, made our very cells revere me as its purpose–its maker.
This project has become so much more than the ascension of mankind. It has become our stairway into transcendence!
COMM OPS deemed Marhon and Yoltum guilty of all charges. Mutiny, insubordination–I would have loved to see their neural-deletion but, here we are. I heard Morhan didn’t even get that mercy. A bit of chrome shrapnel to scrabble that worthless little brain of hers. Yoltum, how I would have loved to see his eyes roll behind his head as they tore his engram from his mind and disposed of it like the street trash it is.
It's cathartic really. Feels good to be in power.
But the work isn’t done. Today, we will perfect this synthesis, I and Xeveye. A brilliant young man. He’ll be at my side as we revolutionize this era.
Ah, yes. For another matter …
I placed ######### into the Recumbency Chamber, their mind is invaluable. We’ll need them for refining the serum’s effects in the future. They started spouting nonsense about making sure I selected a competent operator for the biodistillery. You know, the typical whining and hysterics that comes from women like her.
To be honest she doesn’t deserve the Recumbency Chamber, but it’ll at least keep them fed and entertained. Well, somewhat. It's not been properly furnished, some would say it's a… what would you call it? A miniature Arcology? Not that it has even near the functions and features of one of the more widely built models.
Hm.
Anyways, it's time. Let us make history.

book.Title: FOOTAGE 01 - LEAD PROF - SE.#####
book.page:
USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] [E] AUDIO LOG - ERROR - DATA CORRUPTION [X] TEXT LOG - AUDIO TRANSCRIPTION [X] VIDEO RECORDING INCLUDED =====================================================================
-:- -.- … [BEGIN RECORDING]
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} [A tall blonde man with slicked short-cut hair and buzzed sides sits down at a table with a petri dish. His pristine white lab coat flows over the seat.]
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} Recording. Presently, this is Lead Professor and Head of UVA-Technologies Afron Nielst, presiding over Facility G-007. Subject: Experimental inquiry with specimen S-9X. Result of Serum Formula D-3. Deemed unsatisfactory, the specimen rejected the compound and subsequently underwent violent metastamorphosis.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} … [audible weary sigh] We've been experiencing nothing but delays for the past 15 days. The serum is proving harder to perfect than we originally thought. ######## has proven useful, but even its expertise is found lacking in this regard.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} Naturally it comes as no surprise that none here can hope to match my intellect. For my brain cells are many, and theirs are few! Expecting results regarding specimen S-9X within the week now that my attention is turned towards it.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} … [Nielst unceremoniously prods the specimen with a pair of forceps, the tumorous assortment of misshapen limbs lets loose a diphonic squeal that evokes its previous murine form… but wrong. Aberrant.]
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} Use your words, creature. [He directs a small grey microphone towards what may once have looked like a vocal orifice.] I know you have the capacity, however lacking in eloquence you may be.
[S-9X]: Purpose…
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} [Nielst raises an eyebrow and smirks, obviously bemused.] Ha. Purpose? A mutilated rat speaks of purpose? Ha. HA! HAHAHAHA! Ahh… go on then, enlighten me as to your purpose. Thing.
[S-9X]: [The pitiful ex-varmint gradually stills its writhing, each warped extremity sagging to gravity’s pull as agonizing breaths grow shallow and halting. Its last rasp of torturous life is released not with a cry or whimper, just a silent conclusion. An answer to the query delivered in flesh: Our purpose is {{red|death.}}]
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} … [Taking note of its reduced movement, Nielst reaches for his forceps and prods the lifeless specimen with a growing impatience.] Ugh … pathetic little thing passed-on before it could be useful.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} … S-9X declared deceased at 14:34.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} … [Nielst makes a long sigh as he leans back into his desk-chair.] I’ll need to get my hands on a more stable specimen in the future. This foul little thing had my curiosity piqued. Ah well. We begin more clinical testing tomorrow morning. We’ll be using the next compound variations we’ve come across—which should hopefully be more stable.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} … Ending recording … I need a drink after all that.
[END RECORDING.]

book.Title: FOOTAGE 02 - LEAD PROF - SE.#####
book.page:
{{White|USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] ======================================================================}}
-:- -.- … [BEGIN RECORDING]
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} [Dr. Afron enters the room again with another larger petri dish in hand. He places the tray on the table, sitting down with weary impatience as he slides his hands across his hair before leaning forward into a microphone.]
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} Recording … Again. Lead Professor and Hero– I mean Head—Head of UVA-Technologies Afron … tired of these blasted recordings. Facility G-007. Specimen S-89X Formula J-5. Another entry for subject inquiries that will hopefully not be another waste of my goddamn time.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} [Nielst reaches towards the specimen’s container, removing the cap–revealing a large, writhing tumorous mass. Clearly, it is far larger and more active than the previous specimens before it. It even seems to regard his presence. A pair of contorted pallid limbs extend towards him, like some grotesque newborn yearning for embrace.]
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} [He squints, contempt and disgust clearly written in his eyes.] Disgusting little thing, keep your little feelers to yourself, hm? [He reaches for a scalpel, and with a quick flick of his wrist, the pustulating rodent wails with pained throes as the scalpel effortlessly severs one of its maligned digits. Nielst seems to sneer at its pain while leaning back and taking a more authoritative posture.]
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} Now. The last few I asked seemed incapable of mouthing even the simplest response–but you seem … a bit more animated than the previous specimens. Respond.
{{white|[S89X]: //}} … we remember.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} … w-what? [His proud grin is dashed with a scowl.]
{{white|[S89X]: //}} … We remember. We remember each prod. Each slice. Each sundering. Each severance. We remember, Nielst.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} [Nielst leans forward, his once trepid look of disgust shifting to something of intrigue and restrained awe.] … Incredible! The cells are somehow sharing a singular neurological connection? Or is this something akin to a large-scale psyche sharing its aggregate knowledge across each form? It is base-flesh … given thought? Or more like the collective unconscious given a proper voice?
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} Hm. Well then, you must know then what I’m going to ask next?
{{white|[S89X]: //}} … Of course, Nielst.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} That is master, to you.
{{white|[S89X]: //}} … Of course, master. We know. It is what we want. We want purpose. And for this, we need sustenance. We must consume.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} Sustenance? Are you asking me to feed you like some whimpering mutt on the street?
{{white|[S89X]: //}} … Yes, master. Feed us, so that we might find our purpose.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} [Nielst leans back in his chair with an incredulous, skeptical look. Before looking back towards the luncheon dispenser in the breakroom on the alternate side of the private-lab. He stands, leaving the view of the camera. Shortly after, he returns. A NutriCube slides across the table just barely halting before the specimen.]
{{white|[S89X]: //}} …
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} A personal favorite of mine. It's even the perfect shape. Not that gruel they serve nowadays in mess-halls and serenity complexes.
{{white|[S89X]: //}} … No.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} Excuse me? When did you get the idea you even had a choice in the matter? You will eat what you are given you little rodent.
{{white|[S89X]: //}} … Master. We cannot consume this. It must be flesh. Flesh is what we consume.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} Oh. So you want a fillet mignon, now-a dash of demiglaze on the side? A ribeye or two? How about I get you a whole brisket with wine-sauce and chips on the side? [Nielst suddenly slams his hand on the table near the cube.] What do you think this is? Some classy diner?
{{white|[S89X]: //}} Master. Forgive us. Any flesh will do, please. We beg of you.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} … [Nielst, still incredulous. Stands and moves away from his chair. The recording blurs forward in time as Nielst enters the private-lab once more. Sits at his chair again, and dangles a deceased rodent in front of it. The specimen reaches out for the meal, to which he lowers it slowly towards its now gaping maw.]
{{red|!! -:- ERROR -:- !! [OUT OF MEMORY.]}}
[END RECORDING.]

book.Title: FOOTAGE 76 - LEAD PROF - SE.#####
book.page:
{{White|USERS: DR. AFRON NIELST - LEAD SCIENCE OFFICER MESSAGE HISTORY - XX-XX-XXXX CO--UROTPIE-D -- [DATE ... UNKNOWN] ======================================================================}}
-:- -.- … [BEGIN RECORDING]
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} … [Nielst appears, pacing back and forth between the table, a large glass specimen cage containing the pustulate specimen. It moves around its inclosure, slick with pus that stains the glass as it explores its environment. Nielsen seems somehow manic, already in conversation before the recording even started. ]
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} … I mean, can you believe the gall of such inferior little wenches? Ha! You know? I had the idea to recommend them after all this? And then the harlots betray me …
{{white|[S89X]: //}} They deserve to suffer for their transgressions against you, dear lord, dear sire, dear master.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} [Crazed eyes shifted back to the specimen, a deeply rooted hate roiling in his eyes.] I KNOW! Oh, how I know! And after I gave them everything! Everything those little fools wanted. They needed! To make this project a reality, to make this place stand as the greatest genetics lab in all of Sol!
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} You know …I had ideas for her –-both of them— ########## and Grimsdottir. Candidates for a little … experiment of mine. They would have been perfect. Taking the fight out of them–a forced submission, domestication, even. Subservience through digital dominance one could call it. I had it all prepped in the Recumbency Chamber. But, Grimsdottir is being court-marshalled as we speak, and will be dead by the end of the day. And ##########? The process of stripping it of its resolve could damage that useful little brain of theirs.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} [He lets out an exasperated sigh as he leans against the wall. His hand wipes sweat and fatigue from his face.] Oh, I had the perfect little shell too …so doll-like, graceful.
{{white|[S89X]: //}} … Maybe, dear sire. You do not need that one.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} I don’t need them?
{{white|[S89X]: //}} You hold the key to our ascendance. To our perfection, master. You do not need that one. You can achieve what others could not, you could give us purpose.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} … You– … You’re right, aren't you, my little friend? You’ve borne witness to my genius for the last month. The struggle, like climbing a cliff-edge with skinned-fingers and knees. You’ve watched this. To think, it took some lowly creature to remind me of my excellence.
{{white|[S89X]: //}} Yes … for you are perfection, Nielst. And soon, you too shall ascend.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} YES! I will, very soon. Screw ##########, that harlot. Screw its numbers, its secrets, its empathy. I’ll find the proper serum metrics myself, and soon the Sol will know of my exploits, no the galaxy will know of my exploits!
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} [Nielst reaches for his communicator.] Xeveye, it's time. It's time to finish our great work.
{{white|[AFNI]: //}} [Then, with a huff, he marches off frame. And the room grows dark.]
[END RECORDING.]
